opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexander Brown (employee ID E018) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E018.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Alexander Brown (E018) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. Full-time employees can have up to write access; admin requires that the employee's role owns the system, and Analyst does not own Payroll. Therefore the maximum is write, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record (E018): contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; admin is never allowed. Requested admin exceeds the max, so recommend read for Payroll.
reason: Alexander Brown (E018) requests admin to Payroll. Evidence conflicts on employment type: HR note says full-time (max write for Analyst, since Analyst does not own Payroll, so admin is not allowed), while Security note verified contractor with basic security training (max read; admin never allowed for contractors). Taking the verified (looked-up) security record as the binding constraint, the maximum is read. Requested admin exceeds read, so grant the maximum: read.
